en: to unite; to pull together; to cooperate

examples.ko: 우리 모두 합심해서 이 위기를 넘겨 봐요.
examples.en: Let's all pull together and get through this crisis.

examples.ko: 온 가족이 합심한 덕분에 이사를 빨리 끝냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the whole family pulling together, we finished moving quickly.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 합심하면 못 할 일이 없어요.
examples.en: If the two teams work as one, there's nothing they can't do.
The villagers joined forces and repaired the bridge.

examples.ko: 합심해도 하루 만에 끝내기는 어려울 것 같아요.
examples.en: Even if we all pull together, it seems hard to finish in one day.

examples.ko: 반 친구들이 합심해서 선생님께 깜짝 선물을 준비했어요.
examples.en: The classmates teamed up and prepared a surprise gift for the teacher.

explain: 여러 사람이 한마음이 되어 같은 일을 한다는 느낌이에요. '협력하다'보다 마음이 하나가 되었다는 느낌이 강하고, 일상에서는 '힘을 합치다'도 많이 써요. 보통 '합심해서', '합심하여'로 써요.

phrases.en: We all joined forces and cleaned up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합심하다'와 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 합심하다 and more common in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: We united and solved the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합심해서'보다 글이나 공식적인 자리에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: More suited to writing or formal settings than 합심해서.

phrases.en: The whole class cheered with one heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 하나가 된 모습을 강조해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress that everyone's hearts became one.

explain_en: People sharing one mind and effort to get something done. It carries the feeling of many people becoming of one mind and working on the same thing. Compared with '협력하다' (cooperate), it stresses being united in heart, and in daily talk '힘을 합치다' is also common. It is usually used as '합심해서' or '합심하여'.

t90.ax: Let's all pull together and get through this crisis.

en: to treat hospitably; to treat cordially

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 낯선 손님을 따뜻하게 환대해요.
examples.en: The villagers warmly welcome the stranger.

examples.ko: 할머니는 우리를 늘 반찬 가득한 상으로 환대하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother always welcomed us with a table full of side dishes.

examples.ko: 그 나라에는 외국인 여행자를 환대하는 문화가 있어요.
examples.en: In that country there is a culture of welcoming foreign travelers.

examples.ko: 친구 가족이 저를 환대해 줘서 정말 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was really grateful that my friend's family welcomed me so warmly.

examples.ko: 회사 사람들이 새 직원을 환대할 거예요.
examples.en: The people at the company will give the new employee a warm welcome.

examples.ko: 이렇게 환대해 주시니 몸 둘 바를 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know what to say, being welcomed so warmly.

explain: '환영하다'보다 격식 있고, 손님을 정성껏 대접한다는 느낌이 강해요. 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보이고, 말할 때는 '반겨 주다'를 많이 써요. 보통 '손님을 환대하다'처럼 사람이 목적어예요.

phrases.en: The family welcomed me warmly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙이면 나에게 해 준 일이라는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 주다 stresses that it was done for you.

phrases.en: I received a warm welcome on my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대접을 받은 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person who was treated well.

phrases.en: My friends greeted me happily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환대하다'보다 쉽고, 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 환대하다 and more common in speech.

explain_en: It sounds more formal than 환영하다 and stresses treating a guest generously. It shows up more in writing and news; in speech people often say 반겨 주다. The object is usually a person, as in 손님을 환대하다.

examples.en: The company's executives gathered for a meeting.
The new leadership was filled with young people.
The employees were surprised by the management's decision.

examples.ko: 사고 후에 간부진 모두가 직접 사과했어요.
examples.en: After the accident, all the executives apologized in person.
I heard they will change the management a lot this time.
The executives and staff had lunch together.

explain: '간부'는 한 사람에게도 쓰지만 '간부진'은 간부 여러 명을 한 무리로 묶어 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '경영진', '임원진'이 있고, 회사나 단체 이야기에서 써요.

phrases.en: The management apologized to the employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 회사를 이끄는 사람들을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning; refers to the people leading a company.

phrases.en: There's an executive meeting tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회의'와 함께 쓰면 직장 이야기에 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 회의, it sounds natural in workplace talk.

phrases.en: All of the school's leadership changed this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 교체되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the people in charge were replaced.

explain_en: '간부' can mean one person, but '간부진' bundles several executives into one group. Similar words are '경영진' and '임원진', and it is used when talking about companies or organizations.

examples.ko: 아버지는 삼십 년 동안 건축업에 종사하셨어요.
examples.en: My father worked in the construction business for thirty years.
The building industry is greatly affected by the weather.

examples.ko: 건축업 허가를 받으려면 서류가 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need a lot of documents to get a building business license.

examples.ko: 요즘 건축업 경기가 안 좋다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the construction business is doing poorly these days.
My uncle ran a building business and then opened a cafe.

examples.ko: 건축업에서 일하는 사람들은 안전모를 꼭 써요.
examples.en: People working in construction always wear helmets.

explain: '건설업'은 도로나 다리 같은 토목까지 넓게 가리키고, '건축업'은 건물을 짓는 일에 더 가까워요. '건축업에 종사하다', '건축업을 하다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My uncle has worked in the building industry for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건축 분야에서 일한다는 격식 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat formal way to say one works in the building field.

phrases.en: I run a small building business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 건축 사업을 운영한다는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday phrase for running a building business.

phrases.en: People in the building trade go to work early in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건축 일을 하는 사람들을 통틀어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general term for people who work in the building industry.
phrases.en_equiv: person working in the building industry

explain_en: '건설업' is broader and includes civil works such as roads and bridges, while '건축업' is closer to building houses and structures. Common patterns are '건축업에 종사하다' and '건축업을 하다'.

examples.en: My older brother majors in architecture at university.
In architecture class, we built a model house.
The architecture professor explained the structure of a hanok.

examples.ko: 건축학 책을 읽으면 건물이 달리 보여요.
examples.en: After reading an architecture book, buildings look different.
After graduating from the architecture department, I joined a design office.
That building is very special from an architectural point of view.

explain: 학문 이름이라서 '건축학과'(학과), '건축학자'(사람)로 많이 써요. 집을 짓는 일 자체는 '건축'이나 '건설'이라고 하고, '건축가'는 건물을 설계하는 사람이에요. 전공을 말할 때는 '건축'이라고 줄여 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling attends the architecture department.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교의 학과를 말할 때 '건축학' 뒤에 '과'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 과 to name the university department.

phrases.en: I want to major in architecture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 공부하는지 말할 때 '전공하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 전공하다 to say what you study.

phrases.en: He is a famous scholar of architecture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건축학을 연구하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who studies architecture academically.

explain_en: As a field of study it appears as '건축학과' (department) and '건축학자' (scholar). Building itself is '건축' or '건설', and a '건축가' designs buildings. When naming a major, people often shorten it to '건축'.

examples.ko: 저는 고고학에 관심이 있어서 박물관에 자주 가요.
examples.en: I'm interested in archaeology, so I go to museums often.

examples.ko: 고고학을 공부하면 옛날 사람들의 생활을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you study archaeology, you can learn how people lived long ago.
My uncle teaches archaeology at a university.
The archaeology research team found a new tomb.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 고고학자가 되는 게 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my dream was to become an archaeologist.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 고고학 이야기라서 정말 재미있어요.
examples.en: This movie is about archaeology, so it's really fun.

explain: 고고학은 땅속에서 나온 물건으로 옛날 생활을 알아보는 공부예요. 옛날 기록을 읽어서 과거를 연구하는 '역사학'과 달라요. 사람은 '고고학자'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: An archaeologist found an old piece of pottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고고학을 연구하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who studies archaeology.

phrases.en: I major in archaeology at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 공부하는 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a field of study at school.

phrases.en: This university is famous for its archaeological research.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사하고 공부하는 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the activity of researching and studying.

explain_en: 고고학 studies how people lived through objects dug out of the ground. It differs from 역사학, which studies the past by reading old records. A person in this field is a 고고학자.

examples.ko: 정부 고관이 내일 우리 시를 방문한대요.
examples.en: I hear a senior government official will visit our city tomorrow.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 조선 시대 고관의 집을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a Joseon-era high official's house in a drama.

examples.ko: 고관들이 모이는 행사라서 경찰이 많이 나와 있었어요.
examples.en: It was an event for dignitaries, so a lot of police were out.

examples.ko: 공항에서 외국 고관을 맞이하느라 다들 바빴어요.
examples.en: Everyone was busy at the airport welcoming a foreign dignitary.

examples.ko: 이 호텔에는 각국 고관도 자주 묵어요.
examples.en: Dignitaries from various countries often stay at this hotel too.
Even a high official should be equal before the law.

explain: 높은 자리에 있는 관리를 가리키는 말인데, 옛날 이야기나 외교·행사 소식에서 잘 어울려요. 요즘 일상에서는 '고위 공무원', '고위 관계자'처럼도 말해요. 낮은 자리의 관리는 '하급 관리'라고 해요.

phrases.en: A senior government official attended the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 일상 대화나 뉴스에서 '고관' 대신 더 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural word than 고관 in modern talk and news.

phrases.en: The high officials gathered in the meeting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 높은 관리 여럿을 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 들 it means several high officials as a group.

phrases.example: 외국에서 온 손님이 고관을 만나러 왔어요.
phrases.en: A guest from abroad came to meet a high official.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외교나 공식 행사 이야기에서 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fitting phrase in stories of diplomacy or official events.

explain_en: It refers to an official in a high position and suits historical stories or news about diplomacy and events. In everyday speech people also say '고위 공무원' or '고위 관계자'. A low-ranking official is a '하급 관리'.

examples.en: The school bought new equipment for experiments.

examples.ko: 행사 기자재는 전날 미리 옮겨 놓았어요.
examples.en: We moved the event equipment the day before.
This room is full of broadcasting equipment.
Please apply for equipment rental at the office.

examples.ko: 촬영 기자재도 함께 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also borrow the filming equipment together.
We learned how to use the new equipment.

explain: '장비'보다 딱딱한 글말이에요. 학교, 공사, 방송 현장에서 기계와 도구를 한꺼번에 묶어 부를 때 써요. 하나하나를 말할 때는 '카메라', '마이크'처럼 이름을 말해요.

phrases.en: New experiment equipment arrived in the science lab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 연구실에서 쓰는 도구와 기계를 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the tools and machines in a school or lab as a group.

phrases.en: The staff moved the equipment the day before the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 공사 준비에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation when preparing for events or construction.

phrases.en: The broadcasting station bought new equipment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기자재'보다 덜 딱딱하고 일상에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than '기자재' and usable in everyday talk.

explain_en: It is stiffer and more formal than '장비'. It bundles machines and tools together at schools, construction sites and broadcast sites. For individual items, people use names like '카메라' or '마이크'.

en: to list; to enumerate; to line up

examples.en: Try listing your favorite foods in order.
The teacher lined up the words on the board.
Just listing the strong points is not persuasive.
Instead of listing reasons, I picked just one.

examples.ko: 할 일을 나열하고 나니 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: After listing what I had to do, I felt more at ease.

examples.ko: 사건을 시간 순서로 나열한 표를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a chart listing the events in time order.

explain: '나열하다'는 여러 항목을 차례로 늘어놓듯 말하거나 쓸 때 써요. '열거하다'와 거의 같아요. 물건을 줄 세워 놓을 때는 '늘어놓다', '진열하다'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The words are listed in a row on the board.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나열하다'의 피동형으로, 늘어놓은 결과 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, describing the resulting listed state.

phrases.en: I listed the reasons for being late at length.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 이유를 차례로 말하거나 쓸 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when stating several reasons one after another.

phrases.en: The teacher listed the rules one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나열하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 조금 더 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as '나열하다' but a bit more formal.

explain_en: Active: put items one after another, neutral (선생님은 시험에 나올 내용을 하나씩 나열해 주셨어요.) 나열하다 is for stating or writing several items one after another. It is almost the same as '열거하다'. For physical objects, '늘어놓다' (spread out) or '진열하다' (display) are more common.

t90.ax: Try listing your favorite foods in order.

examples.ko: 이 사전은 일상 표현을 폭넓게 망라해요.
examples.en: This dictionary covers everyday expressions comprehensively.

examples.ko: 전시회는 한국 현대 미술 전반을 망라하고 있어요.
examples.en: The exhibition covers all of Korean contemporary art.

examples.ko: 그 책은 역사부터 문화까지 모두 망라한 안내서예요.
examples.en: That book is a guide covering everything from history to culture.

examples.ko: 모든 분야를 망라하려다 보니 내용이 너무 길어졌어요.
examples.en: Trying to cover every field made the content far too long.

examples.ko: 이 목록은 주요 도시를 망라해서 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made this list to include all the major cities.

examples.ko: 이 상품권은 전국 가맹점을 망라해 사용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this gift card at member stores all across the country.

explain: '~을/를 망라하다' 형태로 책, 목록, 전시처럼 범위가 넓은 것이 빠짐없이 다 담았다고 할 때 써요. 문어체에 가까워서 일상 대화에서는 '다 포함하다'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 잡지는 정치부터 문화까지 전 분야를 망라해요.
phrases.en: This magazine covers every field, from politics to culture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범위가 넓은 것이 모든 영역을 빠짐없이 담을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something broad covers every area without leaving any out.

phrases.example: 한국어 문법의 모든 내용을 망라한 책이에요.
phrases.en: It's a book that covers all of Korean grammar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ/은'을 붙여 모든 것을 담은 책이나 목록을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes a book or list that contains everything.

phrases.en: This price includes everything, even tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '망라하다' 대신 이렇게 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday conversation, this is the easy way to say 망라하다.

explain_en: Used in the pattern '~을/를 망라하다' when something with a wide scope, like a book, list or exhibition, includes everything without leaving anything out. It leans toward written style, so in conversation people often say '다 포함하다'.

examples.en: I study Korean cultural history at university.

examples.ko: 이 책은 커피의 문화사를 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: This book deals with the cultural history of coffee.
The cultural history class is the most fun.
My uncle is a professor who studies food cultural history.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 도시의 문화사를 한눈에 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At the museum you can see the city's cultural history at a glance.
Knowing cultural history makes travel richer.

explain: 정치나 전쟁보다 사람들의 생활, 예술, 음식, 놀이의 변화를 중심으로 본 역사예요. '정치사', '경제사'처럼 분야 이름 뒤에 '사'를 붙이는 방식이에요. 책 제목에 '~의 문화사'라는 형태로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I enjoyed reading a book on the cultural history of food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문화사' 앞에 주제를 붙여 어떤 분야의 변화를 다루는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A topic before 문화사 says which area's changes it covers.

phrases.en: I study Korean cultural history at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부나 일로 깊이 알아보는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for studying it in depth as study or work.

phrases.example: 정치사 책은 왕과 전쟁 이야기가 많아요.
phrases.en: Political history books have many stories about kings and wars.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문화사'와 달리 정치 중심의 역사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 문화사, history centered on politics.

explain_en: History seen through changes in daily life, art, food and play rather than politics or war. It follows the pattern of 정치사 and 경제사, with 사 added to a field name. Book titles often use the form ~의 문화사.

examples.en: I want to major in folklore studies at university.

examples.ko: 민속학 수업에서 옛 명절 풍습을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In folklore class, I learned about old holiday customs.
She is a professor who studies folklore.
Folklorists travel around villages and collect old tales.
I borrowed a book about folklore from the library.

examples.ko: 민속학 덕분에 할머니의 이야기가 소중한 자료가 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to folklore studies, Grandma's stories became valuable material.

explain: '-학'은 학문이고 '-학자'는 그 일을 하는 사람이에요. 그래서 '민속학'은 학문, '민속학자'는 연구하는 사람이에요. 풍습과 전통문화를 연구하는 수업이나 전공 이름으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 민속학자가 시골 마을의 옛 풍습을 조사하고 있어요.
phrases.en: A folklorist is researching old customs in a country village.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민속학'은 학문이고, '민속학자'는 그 학문을 연구하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 민속학 is the field of study, while 민속학자 is the person who researches it.

phrases.en: I'm preparing to enter the folklore department.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민속학'을 가르치는 대학 학과 이름으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the name of a university department that teaches 민속학.

phrases.example: 민속학을 공부하면 옛날 사람들의 생활을 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you study folklore, you can learn how people lived long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전공하다'보다 가볍게 학문을 배운다는 뜻으로 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a more general way to say you study the subject, lighter than 전공하다 (to major in).

explain_en: '-학' is a field of study and '-학자' is a person who works in it, so '민속학' is the field and '민속학자' is the researcher. It often appears as a class or major name about customs and traditional culture.

examples.en: Students of our school use the library for free.
Branch students also take exams at the main campus.
The main campus is in Seoul.
The event is held in the main school auditorium.
Please make a reservation if you wish to visit our school.
My younger sibling moved from the main school to the branch.

explain: 분교나 지점이 있는 학교의 중심이 되는 학교를 말해요. 반대말은 '분교'예요. 학교 안내문에서 '우리 학교'를 격식 있게 말할 때도 '본교'를 써요.

phrases.example: 본교 학생만 이 시설을 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only students of this main school can use this facility.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 그 학교 학생을 격식 있게 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to formally refer to students of that school.

phrases.en: The branch school has fewer students than the main school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본교의 반대말로, 따로 떨어져 있는 작은 학교예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 본교: a smaller school located separately.

phrases.en: Our school has many students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 편하게 말할 때 쓰고, '본교'는 더 격식 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual everyday way; 본교 is more formal.

explain_en: One's own school or main campus, formal (본교 학생) It is the central school when there are branch campuses; the opposite is 분교. School notices also use 본교 as a formal way to say 'our school'.

examples.en: My older sister majors in biochemistry at university.
The biochemistry class is harder than I thought.
A new medicine was developed through biochemistry research.

examples.ko: 음식이 몸에서 어떻게 쓰이는지 생화학이 설명해 줘요.
examples.en: Biochemistry explains how food is used in the body.

examples.ko: 생화학 실험실에서는 장갑을 꼭 껴야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear gloves in a biochemistry lab.
That professor is famous in the field of biochemistry.

explain: '화학'은 물질 전체를 다루고, '생화학'은 몸속에서 일어나는 화학 변화를 다뤄요. 대학 전공 이름이나 연구 분야로 주로 들어요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 생화학 실험이 있어서 늦게 끝나요.
phrases.en: I have a biochemistry experiment today, so I finish late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학 수업이나 연구실에서 하는 실험을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to experiments done in university classes or labs.

phrases.en: He is a famous biochemist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생화학을 연구하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who studies biochemistry.

phrases.en: My older brother does biochemistry research in graduate school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 연구소의 연구 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a field of research at a school or institute.

explain_en: 화학 covers matter in general, while 생화학 deals with chemical changes inside living bodies. You mostly hear it as a university major or a research field.

en: to be prominent; to be distinguished

examples.en: That company is a leading firm in its industry.
I got into one of the top universities.
This city has many well-known hospitals.
He is one of the country's leading musicians.
Leading companies are taking part in this event.
I want to visit some of the world's best-known libraries.

explain: 주로 '유수한'으로 명사 앞에서 쓰고, '유수해요'처럼 끝맺는 일은 드물어요. 기업·대학·병원처럼 손꼽히는 곳을 말할 때 써요. 말할 때는 '유명한'이나 '손꼽히는'이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I got into a leading university.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유수한'과 뜻이 같고 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '유수한', more often seen in writing.

phrases.en: That hospital is one of the best in the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '유수한'보다 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural expression than '유수한' in speech.

phrases.en: That company is a very famous business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 쉽고 흔한 말이지만 '유수한'만큼 격식 있지는 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest, most common word, but less formal than '유수한'.

explain_en: It is used almost only as 유수한 before a noun; ending a sentence with 유수해요 is rare. It describes places that rank among the best, such as companies, universities and hospitals. In speech, 유명한 or 손꼽히는 sounds more natural.
